definitions.explanation: The nerve that carries visual signals from the retina to the brain. Used in medical contexts and in explanations of how the eye works.

examples.japanese: {視神経|ししんけい}が{傷|きず}ついている。
{目|め}から{入|はい}った{光|ひかり}は{視神経|ししんけい}を{通|とお}って{脳|のう}に{届|とど}く。
examples.english: Light entering the eye travels through the optic nerve to the brain.

examples.japanese: {緑内障|りょくないしょう}は{視神経|ししんけい}が{少|すこ}しずつ{損|そこ}なわれていく{病気|びょうき}だ。
examples.english: Glaucoma is a disease in which the optic nerve is gradually damaged.

notes:
Formed from {視|し} (sight) plus {神経|しんけい} (nerve). The same pattern names the other cranial nerves: {聴神経|ちょうしんけい} (auditory nerve), {嗅神経|きゅうしんけい} (olfactory nerve).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {視神経|ししんけい}が{傷|きず}つく: for the optic nerve to be damaged
- {視神経|ししんけい}を{圧迫|あっぱく}する: to press on the optic nerve
- {視神経|ししんけい}{炎|えん}: optic neuritis

USAGE:
Unlike {神経|しんけい} on its own, which is freely used figuratively ({神経|しんけい}が{細|こま}かい, sensitive), {視神経|ししんけい} stays literal and anatomical.
